_comment: THE CACHE INDEX FOR THE STEEL CENSUS, brief 8 sector 3. One entry per fetch: the URL,
the day, the byte count and the SHA-256 of what came back. Bodies are held beside this
file under their hash and are NOT committed -- the index is the part that makes a claim
checkable, and it holds no publisher's text.
THE THREE BENCHMARK FILES ARE INDEXED HERE TOO, as fetches with no http status: they were
retrieved by hand past a registration form. Their hashes are the snapshot -- see
MOVED HERE 15 September 2026, and the reason is worth keeping. steel_search.py was copied
from ccs_search.py with a text substitution that replaced the string 'sources/cache/ccs'
and MISSED the path built from separate quoted segments, so the first steel fetches wrote
into the cement-and-CCS index. Caught when a later read looked for the steel index and
found none. The entries are moved rather than re-fetched: they are the same bytes under
the same hashes, and a re-fetch would have recorded a second reading that never happened.
TWENTY RECORDS CARRY `defect` AND `superseded_by`, from 15 September 2026. They are the
UnicodeEncodeError failures that hid twenty of the largest works in Europe: the request was
never sent, so the record says nothing about the publisher. They are kept because this
register does not delete fetches, and each names the successful re-fetch that replaced it.
check_fetch_records.py accepts a defective record only when it carries that supersession.
